clue.text: Portrayal of a Conservative member of nobility

parts.note: a count is a nobleman of continental Europe

explanation.surface: A painting or description of a Tory aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: An account of events is a description or rendering of them, so a portrayal.

clue.text: The whole, for instance, or current chapter symbolic

parts.note: all means the whole of something
taken as written
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Reads like a critic calling an entire work, or one present chapter, symbolic.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegoric work carries a hidden symbolic meaning beneath its literal story.

clue.text: A victory twice curtailed in Rome's central court

indicators.note: curtailed means docked at the tail, and twice means the final letter is removed two times over

parts.note: a triumph is a great victory

explanation.surface: A double win is cut short in a Roman courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice curtailed' drops the last two letters, PH, from TRIUMPH.
explanation.definitionFit: The atrium was the open central hall of a Roman house, around which rooms were arranged.

clue.text: Shakier and more confusing with nothing left out for pair of bishops

indicators.note: out for says one set of letters is taken away and another put in its place

parts.note: woolly thinking is vague and muddled, so woollier means more confusing
O looks like zero, meaning nothing
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so a pair gives two of them

explanation.surface: Something more unsteady and muddled, with a chess pair standing in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out for' swaps O and L (nothing, left) in WOOLLIER for BB.
explanation.definitionFit: Wobbly means unsteady, so the comparative wobblier means less stable, shakier.

clue.text: Twist in fickle men's trust for parts of orchestras

parts.note: to wind is to twist or coil

indicators.note: fickle means changeable, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A twist in the tale of untrustworthy men's faith, oddly about orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: Flutes, oboes, clarinets and horns form the woodwind and brass sections of an orchestra.

clue.text: Gripping experiences, takeover bids

definitions.meaning: a bear hug is a tight, crushing embrace
in finance a bear hug is a takeover offer so generous the target's board can hardly refuse

explanation.surface: Thrilling events and corporate raids side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the phrase: a crushing embrace, and a business offer pitched too high to reject.

clue.text: Maximum permitted amount drunk, describing one male

indicators.note: describing in its geometric sense of drawing a line around, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drink-drive limit described with an inebriated man in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is the geometric sense, drawing around: LIT goes round IM.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is the ceiling, the most that is allowed.

clue.text: Most tranquil in Spain, taking a nap, finally dropping off

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter, and dropping off says it falls away

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: A sleepy Spanish afternoon nap, dozing off at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally dropping off' removes the last A of SIESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy can mean calm and relaxed, so the superlative means the most relaxed.

clue.text: Schoolmate sadly abandoning scruffy sham fur

indicators.note: sadly says the first word's letters are jumbled, abandoning says a scruffy, scrambled set of the last word's letters is thrown out of that pool

explanation.surface: A schoolfriend sadly gives up a shabby fake-fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, H, A, M from SCHOOLMATE ('abandoning'; 'scruffy' says they may come from anywhere), and 'sadly' rearranges the remaining COOLTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelot is the spotted pelt of the South American wild cat, prized as a fur.

clue.text: Stingy lass's narrowly avoided collision

parts.note: near is an old word for mean or stingy
a miss is a girl or lass; the 's stands for 'is' and links to the definition

explanation.surface: A mean girl has just escaped a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an incident where a crash almost happened but did not.

clue.text: What convict doesn't do for affectionate partner?

definitions.meaning: a convict does bird, meaning serves prison time, and does not love doing it
a doting member of a couple

explanation.surface: A wry question about what a prisoner dislikes, set beside a loving mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a prison sentence (from rhyming slang bird-lime, time).
explanation.definitionFit: Lovebirds are small parrots famed for pairing closely, so the word names a fond partner.

clue.text: Tea-party host's break cut originally

indicators.note: originally points at the first letter, and cut says it is chopped off

parts.note: to shatter is to break into pieces

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter's tea break was cut short at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut originally' removes the first letter S from SHATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mad Hatter hosts the famous tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: A local shared tract of land rarely encountered

parts.note: 'un is dialect for 'one', as a local might say 'a good 'un'
a common is a tract of land shared by the community

explanation.surface: A village green that few people ever come across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A local' means 'one' as a dialect speaker says it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon is unusual, seldom met with.

clue.text: Divides cliques taking in good people

indicators.note: taking in means one piece holds the others within it

parts.note: a set is a social clique
men means people, as in men and women

explanation.surface: A society splits into factions that admit only the virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: To segment something is to split it into sections.

clue.text: Coming out of endless crisis with energy

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: an emergency is a crisis
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Escaping an unending disaster with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergence is the act of appearing or surfacing from somewhere.

clue.text: Curiously entailed text giving place and time

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters are oddly ordered

explanation.surface: A strange legal entail written out with a place and date.
explanation.definitionFit: A dateline heads a news report, stating where and when it was filed.

clue.text: Doctrinaire to provide with weapons meeting's president

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
the chair presides over a meeting

explanation.surface: A dogmatic chairman arms the members of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic theorises without practical experience, so the word means theoretical and doctrinaire.

clue.text: Less than complete oratorio — tactless thing to present in troubled times

definitions.text: thing to present in troubled times

indicators.note: less than complete says only part of the words is used, a run concealed within them

explanation.surface: An unfinished oratorio performed tactlessly during a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of oratorio and the start of tactless.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the Riot Act, a formal warning to disperse, is the classic response to unrest.

clue.text: Upset, bicker about the French packages

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top
about means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to scrap is to squabble or fight
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Annoyed, someone argues about French parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes SLECRAP, which 'Upset' turns round: in a down clue, upset reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcels are wrapped items sent by post, that is, packages.

clue.text: Upset ram struggling against current

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrashing about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An agitated ram flounders against a river's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means moving against the flow of a river.

clue.text: Riddles involving western birds

indicators.note: involving in its old sense of wrapping up, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to riddle is to pass through a coarse sieve, to sift

explanation.surface: Puzzles about birds of the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddles' is the verb for sieving, not puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Swifts are fast-flying insect-eating birds.

clue.text: Race is uncivil it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word heard rather than written, so we want a sound-alike

parts.note: coarse means rude or uncivil

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a race, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is run over a set course, and course can mean a race itself.

clue.text: Part of core curriculum to come up repeatedly

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of the basic syllabus keeps coming round.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again and again.

clue.text: Testimony of European study in immorality

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: vice is wickedness, immorality
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A European's private room reveals sordid proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is the testimony or proof given in court.

clue.text: Unfortunately, son, I can't approve

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A parent's regretful refusal to a son's request.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as refusal, but the answer means the opposite: permit.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to authorise or give official permission.

clue.text: Grapple with gear

definitions.meaning: to ... a problem or opponent is to grapple with it

explanation.surface: Wrestling with one's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is both a verb for confronting something and a noun for equipment.

clue.text: Potentially successful projects of pre-eminent theorist now and then

parts.note: star as an adjective means outstanding, pre-eminent

indicators.note: now and then means only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A leading thinker's ventures that may well succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter is a project or idea with a real chance of success, as in 'a non-starter' reversed.
